properties.name: Via Maris
properties.description: The great coastal highway linking Egypt to Mesopotamia along the Mediterranean shore and through the Jezreel Valley, used by armies, traders, and travelers throughout the biblical period.
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: King's Highway
properties.description: The ancient trade route running north-south through Transjordan, connecting the Gulf of Aqaba to Damascus through Edom, Moab, Ammon, and Bashan (Numbers 20:17).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Coastal road to Egypt
properties.description: The Way of Horus / coastal route linking Canaan to Egypt along the northern Sinai coast, likely traveled by the Holy Family and many others fleeing famine or danger.
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Wilderness / Negev route
properties.description: A desert route through the Negev connecting the coastal plain to the Gulf of Aqaba and the Sinai, associated with the wilderness wanderings.
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Ridge Route (Patriarchs' Highway)
properties.description: The hill-country road running along the central watershed ridge through Hebron, Jerusalem, Bethel, Shiloh, and Shechem, the main north-south artery of the highlands where the patriarchs and judges traveled.
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Roman road Antioch - Ephesus
properties.description: A Roman-era overland route across Cilicia and Asia Minor connecting Antioch to the great port city of Ephesus, part of the network Paul used on his missionary journeys.
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Antioch - Damascus - Arabia
properties.description: A Roman-era route linking Antioch to Damascus and onward into Arabia, part of the caravan network Paul references after his conversion (Galatians 1:17).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Damascus Road
properties.description: The route from Jerusalem north through Samaria to Damascus, famous as the road on which Saul of Tarsus encountered the risen Christ (Acts 9:1-9).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Jordan Valley route
properties.description: A north-south route following the Jordan Rift Valley, offering easier passage between Galilee and the Dead Sea region than the surrounding highlands.
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Appian Way (Puteoli to Rome)
properties.description: The famous Roman road from the port of Puteoli to Rome, the final overland leg of Paul's journey to trial before Caesar (Acts 28:13-16).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Caesarea to Rome (sea)
properties.description: A common Roman-era shipping lane across the Mediterranean linking the port of Caesarea Maritima to Rome.
properties.source: Schematic sea lane, not a precise historical track

properties.name: Alexandria to Corinth (sea)
properties.description: A major grain-shipping and trade lane connecting Egypt to Greece, part of the wider Mediterranean maritime network in the Roman period.
properties.source: Schematic sea lane, not a precise historical track

properties.name: Paul's voyage to Malta
properties.description: The storm-driven voyage described in Acts 27, from Caesarea toward Rome via Sidon and Crete, ending in shipwreck on Malta.
properties.source: Schematic sea lane approximating Acts 27; not a precise historical track

properties.name: Antioch to Cyprus voyage
properties.description: The sea route from Seleucia (Antioch's port) to Salamis and Paphos on Cyprus, the first leg of Paul and Barnabas's first missionary journey (Acts 13:4-6).
properties.source: Schematic sea lane, not a precise historical track

properties.name: Via Egnatia (Neapolis to Thessalonica)
properties.description: The great Roman military road across Macedonia from the port of Neapolis through Philippi and Amphipolis to Thessalonica, traveled by Paul on his second missionary journey (Acts 16:11-17:1).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Ephesus to Miletus coastal route
properties.description: The coastal sea route along the Aegean shore of Asia Minor connecting Ephesus, Miletus, and Patara, part of Paul's return journey from his third missionary journey (Acts 20:15-21:1).
properties.source: Schematic sea lane, not a precise historical track

properties.name: Jerusalem to Jericho road
properties.description: The steep descending road through the Judean wilderness between Jerusalem and Jericho, the setting of the Parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:30-37).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Abraham's journey from Ur to Haran
properties.description: Terah and Abram's family migrated northwest from Ur of the Chaldeans along the Euphrates to Haran (Genesis 11:31).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Abraham's journey from Haran to Canaan
properties.description: Abram left Haran at God's call and traveled south through Damascus to Shechem and Hebron in Canaan (Genesis 12:4-6).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Jacob's flight to Haran
properties.description: Fleeing Esau, Jacob traveled from Beersheba north through Bethel and Damascus to his uncle Laban in Haran (Genesis 28:10).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Jacob's return to Canaan
properties.description: After twenty years, Jacob returned from Haran through Peniel and Shechem to Bethel in Canaan (Genesis 31-35).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Joseph's caravan to Egypt
properties.description: Ishmaelite traders carried Joseph from Dothan down the coastal route into Egypt, where he was sold as a slave (Genesis 37:25-36).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: The Exodus route
properties.description: Israel's traditional route from Goshen in Egypt across the Red Sea, through the Sinai wilderness, to Kadesh-barnea and the plains of Moab (Exodus 12-Deuteronomy 34).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Assyrian deportation route
properties.description: The route along which Assyria deported the northern kingdom of Israel from Samaria to cities in Assyria after 722 BC (2 Kings 17:5-6).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Babylonian exile route
properties.description: The route along which Judah was marched into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon after the city fell in 586 BC (2 Kings 25:1-11).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Return from exile
properties.description: The homeward route the exiles took from Babylon back to Jerusalem under Cyrus's decree and later under Ezra and Nehemiah (Ezra 1-2; Nehemiah 2).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: The Queen of Sheba's journey
properties.description: The Queen of Sheba's long caravan journey from southern Arabia to Jerusalem to see Solomon's wisdom and wealth (1 Kings 10:1-13).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Elijah's journey to Horeb
properties.description: Fleeing Jezebel, Elijah traveled from Beersheba into the wilderness to Horeb, where he encountered the still small voice of God (1 Kings 19:1-8).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Jonah's journey to Nineveh
properties.description: After being cast up on shore, Jonah traveled overland from the coast near Joppa to Nineveh to preach repentance (Jonah 1-3).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: The Magi's journey
properties.description: Wise men from the East followed a star from the region of Babylon/Persia to Bethlehem to worship the newborn Jesus (Matthew 2:1-12).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: The Holy Family's flight to Egypt
properties.description: Warned in a dream, Joseph took Mary and the infant Jesus from Bethlehem through Gaza to Egypt to escape Herod (Matthew 2:13-15).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: The Holy Family's return to Nazareth
properties.description: After Herod's death, the Holy Family returned from Egypt and settled in Nazareth in Galilee (Matthew 2:19-23).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Philip's road to Gaza
properties.description: The desert road from Jerusalem to Gaza where Philip met and baptized the Ethiopian eunuch (Acts 8:26-40).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Peter's journey from Joppa to Caesarea
properties.description: Peter traveled from Joppa to Caesarea to meet Cornelius, a turning point in the early church's mission to Gentiles (Acts 10).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Paul's 1st journey: Perga to Antioch of Pisidia
properties.description: Paul and Barnabas traveled inland from Perga up into the highlands to Antioch of Pisidia (Acts 13:13-14).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Paul's 1st journey: the Galatian cities
properties.description: From Antioch of Pisidia, Paul and Barnabas preached in Iconium, Lystra, and Derbe (Acts 13:51-14:6).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Paul's 1st journey: the return leg
properties.description: Paul and Barnabas retraced their steps through the Galatian cities and back down to Perga and Attalia to sail home (Acts 14:21-25).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Paul's 2nd journey: overland to Troas
properties.description: On his second journey, Paul traveled overland from Antioch through Derbe, Lystra, and Galatia before being directed to Troas (Acts 15:41-16:8).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Paul's 2nd journey: Berea to Corinth
properties.description: Paul went from Berea to Athens, where he preached at the Areopagus, and on to Corinth (Acts 17:10-18:1).
properties.source: Schematic sea lane, not a precise historical track

properties.name: Paul's 3rd journey: Antioch to Ephesus
properties.description: Paul began his third journey overland from Antioch through the Galatian and Phrygian region to Ephesus (Acts 18:23-19:1).
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Paul's 3rd journey: Ephesus to Corinth
properties.description: After three years in Ephesus, Paul sailed by way of Troas and Macedonia to Corinth (Acts 20:1-2).
properties.source: Schematic sea lane, not a precise historical track

properties.name: Paul's 3rd journey: Corinth back to Troas
properties.description: Paul returned from Corinth through Macedonia to Troas, where he raised Eutychus from the dead (Acts 20:3-12).
properties.source: Schematic sea lane, not a precise historical track

properties.name: Paul's 3rd journey: Troas to Miletus
properties.description: Paul sailed down the Aegean coast from Troas by way of Assos, Mitylene, Chios, and Samos to Miletus, where he addressed the Ephesian elders (Acts 20:13-38).
properties.source: Schematic sea lane, not a precise historical track

properties.name: Paul's 3rd journey: Patara to Jerusalem
properties.description: Paul's final leg to Jerusalem, sailing from Patara by way of Tyre and Ptolemais to Caesarea, then overland to Jerusalem (Acts 21:1-17).
properties.source: Schematic sea lane, not a precise historical track

properties.name: Phoenician route: Tyre to Tarshish
properties.description: The far-western Mediterranean sea lane Phoenician traders used to reach Tarshish, the destination Jonah fled toward (Jonah 1:3; Ezekiel 27:12).
properties.source: Schematic sea lane, not a precise historical track

properties.name: Trade route to Ophir
properties.description: Solomon's ships sailed from Ezion-geber on the Red Sea to Ophir for gold and precious goods (1 Kings 9:26-28).
properties.source: Schematic sea lane, not a precise historical track

properties.name: Incense Route
properties.description: The great overland trade route carrying frankincense and myrrh from southern Arabia north through Petra to Gaza and the Mediterranean.
properties.source: Schematic route, not a precise archaeological trace

properties.name: Nile River corridor
properties.description: Egypt's central artery of travel and trade along the Nile between Memphis and Thebes, mentioned throughout the biblical narratives set in Egypt.
properties.source: Schematic river corridor, not a precise historical track

properties.name: Euphrates River corridor
properties.description: The Euphrates river corridor linking Babylon to Mari and Haran, the great highway of Mesopotamian civilization and trade.
properties.source: Schematic river corridor, not a precise historical track
